new_symbol_range_suggestions.selection_coefficient: nonnegative initial state; e.g. 0 to 2 as an initial effective selection scale
new_symbol_range_suggestions.selection_capacity: positive; e.g. small to moderate positive selection scale comparable to initial selection_coefficient

derivation_notes: The constant-selection assumption is relaxed by treating the effective viability advantage as an internal state that decays through a finite-capacity saturation law, representing depletion or saturation of the context that sustains the advantage. The initial condition for selection_coefficient should be the intended starting selective advantage and is nondegenerate because selection_coefficient=0 would lie on an invariant zero-effect set with no allele-frequency change.
change_summary: The favored allele still follows genic selection, but the selection coefficient is no longer fixed: it now relaxes downward over time with a saturating decay term. This preserves the parent law in the slow-relaxation limit while creating observable late-time slowdown in p that cannot be captured by one constant logistic gain.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The selective advantage is positive and constant through time.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Time-dependent decay of effective viability selection due to environmental depletion, diminishing resource contrast, or saturation of the advantage-conferring context.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent by taking selection_decay_rate -> 0, so selection_coefficient remains constant during the experiment.

response_change.parent_relation: With one constant selection_coefficient, dp_dt is a fixed logistic function of p, symmetric about p=0.5 up to a global gain and with a single invariant saturation scale set only by p(1-p).
response_change.child_relation: Let selection_coefficient relax over time as the selective environment is depleted or adaptation saturates, so dp_dt depends on both p and the evolving strength of selection; the p-to-dp_dt relation bends over during a trajectory rather than remaining a single shared logistic shape.
response_change.observable_effect: For trajectories started at the same initial p but observed over longer time windows, the favored allele initially rises nearly as in the parent but later slows more than any single constant-coefficient logistic law predicts, producing reduced late-time slope and altered cumulative curvature.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when selective advantage is not sustained indefinitely on the observation timescale, so the characteristic decay time of effective selection is comparable to or shorter than the time required for substantial allele-frequency change; if selection remains effectively constant over the whole experiment, the refinement is not distinguishable.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate-time trajectories would already show slight deviation from a single shared logistic gain; in holdout, longer observation windows or stronger initial selection expose a clearer late-time slowdown from the same depletion mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the relaxation timescale of selection to infinity, so effective selection remains constant during the experiment.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A fixed parameter cannot represent time-dependent erosion of selective advantage within a trajectory. Promoting selection_coefficient to a state is the minimal way to retain the same biological quantity while allowing sustained directional selection to weaken dynamically.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Time-dependent decay of effective viability selection due to environmental depletion, diminishing resource contrast, or saturation of the advantage-conferring context.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored dp_dt keeps the same formal genic factor but is modulated by a hidden state with its own saturating relaxation, so the same observed p can map to different dp_dt at different times within one shared parameterization.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The selective advantage is positive and constant through time.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The effective selective advantage is an internal state that decays over time through a finite-capacity saturation law.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take selection_decay_rate -> 0 so d(selection_coefficient)/dt -> 0 and the initial selection_coefficient is held constant.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding the initial allele frequency fixed and using one shared parameter set, the parent implies dp_dt/(p*(1 - p)) is time-invariant along each trajectory, whereas the child predicts this ratio declines over time as selection_coefficient relaxes. The contrast is visible on sufficiently long trajectories or when initial selection is large enough that the decay state evolves measurably before fixation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single constant parent selection_coefficient can match either the early rise or the late slowdown but not both across trajectories observed over different time windows, because it enforces one time-invariant logistic curvature and a constant per-capita growth ratio dp_dt/(p*(1-p)). Refitting all parent parameters still leaves no mechanism for within-trajectory decay of effective selection.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes the viability advantage is perfectly constant through time, omitting realistic temporal relaxation of the selective differential as the ecological or physiological basis of the advantage is exhausted or saturates.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The selective advantage is positive and constant through time.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Time-dependent decay of effective viability selection due to environmental depletion, diminishing resource contrast, or saturation of the advantage-conferring context.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent target mapping is shortcut by a fixed_environment assumption: once selection_coefficient is set, every trajectory has the same logistic shape in p and differs only by overall timescale. A realistic next refinement is to relax that assumption and let the effective selective advantage decay during the run. Vary the observation window length or, equivalently, compare early versus late portions of trajectories while holding the initial allele frequency fixed at the stated contract and using one shared parameter set across all runs. The parent predicts that the per-capita growth ratio dp_dt/(p(1-p)) is constant in time for all trajectories. The child predicts that this ratio declines over time, so late-time approach toward fixation is slower than the early-time gain would imply. This is a changed target mapping for dp_dt itself, not merely an auxiliary hidden trajectory, because the scored derivative of p changes at the same observed p depending on the history/time through the evolving selection strength. The effect is admissible so long as selection remains nonnegative and decays on an observable timescale; if decay is extremely slow, the parent is approximately recovered. A single refitted constant selection_coefficient cannot reproduce both the early fast rise and the later extra slowdown across such conditions, because it enforces one time-invariant logistic curvature throughout each trajectory.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes the realized viability advantage enters allele-frequency change with a single frequency-independent gain. Here that gain is attenuated by a finite-capacity occupancy state built up by favored carriers, giving a saturating reduction in realized selection that introduces memory and bends the p-to-dp_dt mapping downward at higher prevalence; the nonzero initial occupancy is chosen to avoid an invariant zero-effect branch with no observable feedback.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that selection_coefficient acts as a single gain on p*(1-p). The successor adds a saturating attenuation state generated by the favored allele, so high or sustained p reduces realized selection and shifts the target curvature away from the parent's symmetric logistic response.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The selective advantage is positive and acts linearly on allele-frequency change at all frequencies, apart from the standard p*(1-p) scarcity factor.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Frequency-dependent attenuation of realized viability advantage due to self-limiting ecological context, such as crowding among favored carriers or saturation of the beneficial resource contrast they exploit.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent when attenuation_occupancy/attenuation_capacity is negligible along the trajectory, for example under fast relaxation with weak buildup or in the large-capacity limit attenuation_capacity -> oo.

response_change.parent_relation: At any time, dp_dt is a logistic-in-frequency product p*(1-p) scaled by a single effective selection_coefficient, so the frequency dependence is always symmetric with one fixed interior peak at p=1/2.
response_change.child_relation: Retain positive directional selection but relax the assumption that viability advantage acts linearly in allele frequency; let the realized selection pressure depend on p through a positive saturation or crowding term, so dp_dt remains nonnegative but its frequency-response curvature and peak location shift with p.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with different observed p values while holding the same selection_coefficient trajectory fixed, the child predicts relatively weaker acceleration at high p (or, equivalently, a shifted interior maximum) than the parent's symmetric p*(1-p) law.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories sample a broad interior frequency range, especially moderate-to-high p where a nonlinear realization of the selective advantage can reduce marginal gain relative to the parent while keeping dp_dt nonnegative.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as systematic deviation from a symmetric logistic frequency response over observed p; in holdout, the same mechanism extends that deviation to later times or stronger surviving selection_coefficient values without changing sign.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added frequency-dependent modulation to its linear or weak-effect limit so the realized advantage becomes proportional to selection_coefficient alone.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A new state is needed if the nonlinear realization of selection is interpreted as a slowly varying ecological or physiological occupancy that is built up by the favored allele and feeds back on its realized advantage; existing states alone do not represent that memory effect.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Self-limiting ecological occupancy attenuating realized viability selection
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Frequency-dependent attenuation of realized viability advantage due to self-limiting ecological context, such as crowding among favored carriers or saturation of the beneficial resource contrast they exploit.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the attenuation is a dynamic finite-capacity state coupled to p, so the same instantaneous selection_coefficient can map to different dp_dt depending on occupancy history. That changes the target law itself through a saturating denominator rather than just retuning a shared gain.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The selective advantage is positive and acts linearly on allele-frequency change at all frequencies, apart from the standard p*(1-p) scarcity factor.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The realized viability advantage is attenuated by a finite-capacity occupancy state generated by favored carriers, so selection remains positive but saturates downward as that occupancy accumulates.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when attenuation_occupancy stays negligible relative to attenuation_capacity, including the large-capacity limit or weak-build/fast-relaxation occupancy dynamics.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Across observed trajectories sampling broad interior p, especially sustained moderate-to-high p, the same instantaneous selection_coefficient can produce lower dp_dt after occupancy has accumulated, flattening the high-p side relative to the parent's symmetric p*(1-p) response while keeping dp_dt nonnegative.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast across those conditions because its target mapping is always exactly selection_coefficient times p*(1-p), which fixes the curvature and peak location in p once selection_coefficient is given. Refitting selection_decay_rate and selection_capacity only alters the auxiliary selection_coefficient trajectory and cannot create occupancy-history-dependent attenuation of dp_dt at the same observed p and selection_coefficient.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the favored allele's viability advantage enters dp_dt as a single frequency-independent gain multiplying p*(1-p), even though the ecological realization of that advantage can saturate or be attenuated as the favored type becomes common.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The selective advantage is positive and acts linearly on allele-frequency change at all frequencies, apart from the standard p*(1-p) scarcity factor.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Frequency-dependent attenuation of realized viability advantage due to self-limiting ecological context, such as crowding among favored carriers or saturation of the beneficial resource contrast they exploit.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-gain assumption for how selection_coefficient maps into dp_dt. The parent response is selection_coefficient times a symmetric logistic kernel, so for one shared parameterization it enforces the same curvature and peak location in p across all observed times. A child with frequency-dependent attenuation of realized selection changes the target mapping itself, not just an auxiliary trajectory: for the same observed p and selection_coefficient, dp_dt bends downward more strongly at larger p than the parent predicts. The varied condition is allele frequency along observed trajectories; what is held fixed is the same selection_coefficient trajectory or comparable instantaneous values of selection_coefficient. The qualitative contrast is that the parent always has a symmetric interior response with maximum at p=1/2, whereas the child can shift that peak or flatten the high-p side while preserving nonnegative change and invariant boundaries. This is scientifically admissible when favored carriers begin to dominate the ecological context that created their advantage. If the added mechanism is implemented with negligible strength, or if data only cover a narrow band near p=1/2, the contrast may be weak; otherwise one shared refit of the parent cannot reproduce a systematic p-dependent curvature change because its only frequency dependence is the fixed kernel p*(1-p).

derivation_notes: The attenuation mechanism is re-derived by relaxing the first-order loading assumption and allowing compounding crowding among favored carriers, so realized selection is suppressed by a quadratic load in the dimensionless occupancy ratio. This keeps the same states and parameters but changes the target mapping directly once attenuation_occupancy becomes comparable to attenuation_capacity.
change_summary: The favored-allele growth law now uses a steeper saturating attenuation factor, replacing simple hyperbolic suppression with compounded occupancy suppression. This is a law refinement of the existing attenuation process, not an added evolutionary force.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Occupancy attenuates realized selection through a single linear loading term in the denominator.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Compounding crowding or saturation among favored carriers causes superlinear loss of realized viability benefit once occupancy accumulates, without changing the sign of selection or adding new evolutionary forces.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when the quadratic attenuation contribution is negligible, in particular for attenuation_occupancy/attenuation_capacity << 1 where both laws agree to leading order.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed selection_coefficient, dp_dt increases approximately linearly with p at low favored-allele frequency and is attenuated only by the accumulated occupancy term through a first-order factor 1/(1 + attenuation_occupancy/attenuation_capacity).
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same states but relax the assumption that attenuation is first-order: realized selection falls with a steeper saturating dependence on attenuation_occupancy, so the p-to-dp_dt mapping bends downward more strongly once occupancy becomes comparable to attenuation_capacity.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories or times with matched p and selection_coefficient but different attenuation_occupancy, the decline in dp_dt with occupancy is weak-to-moderate in the parent and sharply compressed after occupancy approaches capacity in the child.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when attenuation_occupancy is driven into the same order as or above attenuation_capacity by sustained occupancy buildup, while p remains in the interior (not near 0 or 1) so logistic limitation does not dominate.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest occupancy already causes some attenuation; in holdout, larger occupancy_load reveals the stronger downward bending of dp_dt that a first-order attenuation law cannot match with one shared parameter set across both low- and high-load regimes.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the generalized attenuation nonlinearity reduces to first-order attenuation, or whenever occupancy_load << 1 so both laws agree to leading order.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: nonlinear occupancy attenuation of viability advantage
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Compounding crowding or saturation among favored carriers causes superlinear loss of realized viability benefit once occupancy accumulates, without changing the sign of selection or adding new evolutionary forces.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the occupancy and capacity are first combined into a dimensionless load and then passed through a nonlinear map with an added quadratic contribution, changing curvature across load regimes rather than merely rescaling amplitude.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Occupancy attenuates realized selection through a single linear loading term in the denominator.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Attenuation reflects compounded crowding so the dimensionless occupancy load enters the realized-selection denominator with both first-order and second-order suppression.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: For attenuation_occupancy/attenuation_capacity << 1, the added quadratic term is subleading and the child approaches the parent attenuation law to leading order.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: When p and selection_coefficient are matched and attenuation_occupancy varies through order-1 multiples of attenuation_capacity, the child predicts nearly parent-like behavior at low occupancy_load but a stronger-than-hyperbolic drop in dp_dt at higher occupancy_load; this is a changed target mapping, not only changed auxiliary trajectories.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both the low-load near-parent slope and the high-load stronger suppression because the parent denominator is affine in occupancy_load, giving one fixed curvature class. Retuning selection_coefficient or attenuation_capacity only rescales where attenuation acts, but cannot create the child’s extra downward bending across both modest and large occupancy_load conditions with one shared parameter set.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes attenuation of the viability advantage is a simple first-order hyperbolic function of occupancy, which can be too weak when self-limiting ecological or physiological crowding compounds at high favored-carrier occupancy.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Occupancy attenuates realized selection through a single linear loading term in the denominator.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Compounding crowding or saturation among favored carriers causes superlinear loss of realized viability benefit once occupancy accumulates, without changing the sign of selection or adding new evolutionary forces.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the mathematical form of the already present attenuation process rather than add a new process. The parent target mapping has a single-gain shortcut: for fixed selection_coefficient, p, and attenuation_capacity, dp_dt depends on attenuation_occupancy through one first-order denominator, so the occupancy effect has a fixed curvature. Vary attenuation_occupancy through its existing dynamics by comparing early versus later times, or parameter settings with different occupancy_buildup_rate and occupancy_relaxation_rate, while holding the rest of the model form fixed. Under admissible conditions where attenuation_occupancy/attenuation_capacity reaches order 1 or larger and p stays away from the boundaries, the child would predict stronger compression of dp_dt at high occupancy than the parent. response_change.parent_relation: With selection_coefficient and attenuation_occupancy fixed at an observed instant, dp_dt is a symmetric logistic-like function of p proportional to p*(1-p), so the rise rate always has a single peak at p=1/2 and equal local slopes at complementary frequencies p and 1-p.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the favored allele's frequency response to directional viability selection is exactly symmetric around p=1/2 after attenuation, which excludes biologically plausible asymmetry in how competitive replacement unfolds across rarity versus commonness.

evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Non-ideal viability competition or replacement can make the favored allele's realized gain depend asymmetrically on competitor availability versus favored-carrier prevalence, shifting the strongest response away from equal frequencies without introducing mutation, migration, or negative selection.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's exact symmetric frequency kernel rather than adding a new process. Hold fixed the current attenuation mechanism and the decaying selection context, and vary the observed allele-frequency position p along trajectories that already satisfy the given initial-condition contract. In the parent, once selection_coefficient and attenuation_occupancy are specified, dp_dt as a function of p is fully determined by one symmetric shape with a peak fixed at p=1/2. A child with an asymmetric but still nonnegative interior frequency kernel changes the target mapping itself, not just auxiliary trajectories: for the same observed selection_coefficient and attenuation_occupancy, the slope and curvature of dp_dt versus p differ and the maximum can occur away from 1/2. This is scientifically admissible in deterministic haploid selection when competitive replacement is not exactly symmetric in rarity and commonness, yet fixation and loss remain invariant and dp_dt stays nonnegative on 0<p<1. The effect is observable only if the sampled trajectories traverse enough of the interior p range; if observations stay very near p=0 or p=1, the contrast weakens. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce a shifted peak location across such conditions because those parameters only rescale the amplitude through selection and attenuation, while the p-shape remains exactly p*(1-p).

derivation_notes: The parent assumed attenuation acts instantaneously from current occupancy alone. Here occupancy first creates a secondary burden through a saturating generation law, and that burden relaxes on its own timescale; choosing delayed_burden(0)=0 gives a non-degenerate initially unexpressed memory branch that activates only after occupancy accumulates, consistent with a delayed damage or deterioration process.
change_summary: I replaced the single-phase instantaneous attenuation by a delayed burden state driven by occupancy. This adds history dependence to dp_dt itself, producing weaker early suppression and stronger later suppression under the same current occupancy when burden has had time to accumulate.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Attenuation responds without memory: the realized viability advantage at time t depends only on the current attenuation_occupancy, not on a lagged accumulated burden generated by past occupancy.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Favored carriers can generate a secondary burden such as toxin accumulation, physiological wear, or local habitat deterioration that integrates occupancy over time and attenuates selection with delay.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces toward the parent when burden_buildup_rate is zero, or when delayed_burden rapidly tracks attenuation_occupancy under a fast-timescale approximation with burden_half_saturation large enough that burden generation is effectively linear over the visited occupancy range.

response_change.parent_relation: The favored allele gain is the product of p(1-p), a time-relaxing selection coefficient, and a monotone attenuation factor that depends only on the current attenuation_occupancy. Thus for fixed p and selection_coefficient, increasing attenuation_occupancy always depresses dp_dt with one fixed attenuation shape.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the instantaneous attenuation law by a delayed physiological/ecological burden that builds from attenuation_occupancy and modulates realized selection after a lag. Then dp_dt at the same current p and attenuation_occupancy can differ depending on accumulated burden history, creating a two-timescale attenuation and altered curvature over time.
response_change.observable_effect: Under matched initial p and similar early occupancy buildup, the child shows an early faster rise in dp_dt followed by a later sharper slowdown once burden accumulates; the parent with one shared parameter set can only attenuate immediately with one phase and cannot reproduce both the weak early suppression and stronger delayed suppression across the same time course.
